title: Colour axis: two hydrogen lines in their right place
claim: Read with the sky-distortion terms off, the wavelength tables put the Paschen-beta and Brackett-alpha lines of the planetary nebula NGC 6543 at their known colours.
test: NGC 6543 in every photo of detector 2 within 0.11 µm of Paschen-beta and of detector 5 within 0.1 µm of Brackett-alpha (76 and 55 photos). Flux in a 3-pixel aperture, background from a ring of 8 to 13.5 pixels; a Gaussian on a straight line is fitted to flux against the wavelength the tables give at the nebula. Expected: the laboratory vacuum wavelength moved by the nebula's velocity of -66 km/s (source of the velocity to be cited before review).
pass_rule: The fitted centre lies within 5 nm of the expected Paschen-beta wavelength and within 15 nm of the expected Brackett-alpha wavelength.
plain: colour checked on two known lines

title: Colour axis: the other four detectors
claim: In detectors 1, 3, 4 and 6 no line of known colour is available to this tool, so the tables are only compared with IRSA's own science wavelength maps. The check rests on IRSA's code and calibration.
test: The tables against the CWAVE layer of IRSA's Spectral WCS product (version cal-swcs-v5-2026-191) at 10,000 random pixels of each detector.
pass_rule: Not a pass or fail test: the largest difference is reported.
plain: colour rests on IRSA's own maps
